Cheyenne Auxiliary Pumping Station located at 1504 Dillon Avenue, Cheyenne, Wyoming for 
sale or lease, with revised terms to facilitate redevelopment and community benefit. Mr. Laybourn 
moved to adopt, seconded by Mr. Moody. Mr. Segrave moved to amend by substitute dated 
December 22, 2025, seconded by Mr. Esquibel. Motion to amend by substitute carried. Voting 
“yes” – all members of the governing body present. Main motion as amended by substitute carried. 
Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body present. Public comment was made by: Maren 
Kallas, Historic Cheyenne Inc. and Milward Simpson, Cheyenne Historic Preservation Board.  
Comments were made by the following members of the governing body: Dr. Aldrich, Mayor 
Collins, Mr. Laybourn and Mr. Segrave. (#6500) 
 
[CA]  RESOLUTION – Designating specified local banks as depositories for municipal funds . 
Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried. (#6501) 
 
[CA] RESOLUTION – Authorizing the Mayor and the City Clerk to sign a Final Plat for Airport 
View, City of Cheyenne, Laramie County, Wyoming (located east of Townsend Place and north 
of and adjacent to Dell Range Boulevard). Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried. (#6502) 
 
 RESOLUTION – Authorizing the Mayor and the City Clerk to sign a Final Plat for Scenic 
Development, 7th Filing, City of Cheyenne, Laramie County, Wyoming (located south of Storey 
Boulevard, west of Converse Avenue, and north of East Carlson Street) . Reporting for Public 
Services Committee, Mr. Segrave moved to adopt, seconded by Dr. Emmons. Mr. Segrave moved 
to amend C ondition (a) to remove the Planning Commission requirement for external access 
easements and revert back to the staff’s original recommendation, seconded by Mr. White. Motion 
to amend carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body present. Main motion as 
amended carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body present with the exception of 
Mr. Moody voting “no”.  Public comment was made by: Jaden Smith, Wasatch Property 
Development. (#6503) 
 
[CA] RESOLUTION – Certifying compliance with Wyoming Statute § 15 -1-402 for the City-
initiated annexation of various tracts of land completely surrounded by current city limits situate 
in North Cheyenne, generally located south of Storey Boulevard, east of Powderhouse Road, north 
of Dell Range Boulevard, and west of Ridge Road. Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried. (#6504) 
 
[CA] RESOLUTION – Authorizing the Mayor and the City Clerk to sign a Final Plat for Golden 
Meadows 2nd Filing, City of Cheyenne, Laramie County, Wyoming (located west of Connie 
Drive, north of Dell Range Boulevard, and east of Golden Meadows Lane) . Motion (per Consent 
Agenda) carried. (#6505) 
  [CA] RESOLUTION – Approving a sponsorship by Bison Beverage for Cheyenne Frontier Days 
events occurring July 17 through July 26, 2026, July 23 through August 1, 2027, and July 21 
through July 30 2028 – referred to Finance Committee. (Sponsor – Mr. Esquibel) 
 
[CA] RESOLUTION – Adopting the amended 2025- 2027 City of Cheyenne Comprehensive 
Consolidated Plan and the amended 2025 Annual Action Plan, as prepared by the Cheyenne 
Housing and Community Development Office, and setting the public comment period and public 
hearings for the plans – referred to Finance Committee. (Sponsor – Mr. Esquibel) 
 
[CA] Memorandum of Understanding between the City of Cheyenne and certain landowners 
regarding annexation of property south of Storey Boulevard, west of Converse Avenue, north of 
Dell Range Boulevard and east of Powderhouse Road. Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried. 
(#8299) 
 
 Memorandum of Understanding by and between Laramie County, the City of Cheyenne, 
the Cheyenne Board of Public Utilities, and the Cheyenne/Laramie County Board of Health 
regarding the management of the ESRI Enterprise Agreement (Various City Funds). Mr. Laybourn 
moved to approve in an amount not to exceed $36,185.00, seconded by Mr. Moody. Mr. Laybourn 
moved to amend by substitute dated December 18, 2025, seconded by Mr. Moody. Motion to 
amend by substitute carried. Voting “yes” –  all members of the governing body present. Main 
motion as amended by substitute  carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body  
present. (#8300) 
 
[CA]  Agreement between the City of Cheyenne and RingCentral, LLC for providing cloud based 
enterprise telecom services for all City departments and divisions – referred to Finance Committee. 
(General Fund) 
 
[CA] Consideration to Purchase between the City of Cheyenne and Motorola Solutions for ten 
(10) Motorola Mobile Radios for the Cheyenne Police Department (2023-2026 Optional 1% Sales 
Tax Fund). Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried (in an amount not to exceed $82,615.90). 
 
[CA] Consideration to Purchase between the City of Cheyenne and Axon Enterprise, Inc. for ten 
(10) In-Car Camera Systems for the Cheyenne Police Department (2023-2026 Optional 1% Sales 
Tax Fund). Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried (in an amount not to exceed $96,974.60). 
 
[CA]  Consideration of Bid #S -7-26 for an Agreement between the City of Cheyenne and Pole 
Mountain Electric, Inc., for the Cheyenne Dunbar Field Light Installation project  – referred to 
Finance Committee. (2021 Specific Purpose Option Tax Fund, Development Impact Fees and Rec 
Mill Grant) 
 
 Transfer of ownership of retail liquor license application filed with the City Clerk’s Office 
for Cheyenne GS, LLC d/b/a Hi Market Cheyenne, 215 E. Lincolnway, Cheyenne, WY (license 
currently held by Scooters Scoreboard, LLC d/b/a Scooters Scoreboard Bar). Mr. Laybourn 
advised there was no recommendation from Finance Committee. Mr. Laybourn moved to approve, 
seconded by Mr. Segrave. Motion failed. Voting “ no” – all members of the governing body  
present. Comment was made by the following member of the governing body: Mayor Collins.   
   Reappointments of Patrick Vann and Patrick Bustos to the Historic Preservation Board; 
Amy Hernandez and Robert Mathia to the Planning Commission; Nick Pickering, Ray Fertig Jr., 
and Julie Goode to the Building Code Board of Appeals; Jeffie Wiggins -McMullen to the Fire 
Civil Service Commission; Carla Winkler to the Police Civil Service Commission; Patti Riesland, 
Julie Tucker and Michelle Woerner to the Mayor’s Council for People with Disabilities; William 
Beaman to the City/County Joint Powers Board for Frontier Park Improvements; and Brian Casey, 
Ryan Gertsch and Travis Shaffer to the Contractor Licensing Board.  Mr. Segrave moved to 
approve, seconded by Mr. White.  Motion carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the governing 
body present with the exception of Mayor Collins  who did not vote (mayoral appointments). 
Comment was made by the following member of the governing body: Mayor Collins. 
 
 Appointments of Jeff White to the Downtown Development Authority Board; Brittany 
Wardle to the City/County Board of Health; Charity Campfield to the Board of Adjustment; Joseph 
Ramos to the Housing and Community Development Board; and John Burdick to the H istoric 
Preservation Board. Dr. Emmons declared a conflict of interest and abstained from voting on the 
item. Mr. Wolfe moved to approve, seconded by Mr. Segrave. Motion carried. Voting “yes” – all 
members of the governing body present with the exception of Mayor Collins  who did not vote 
(mayoral appointments) and Dr. Emmons who also did not vote. 
  
 No comments were made on the Voucher Report as presented. 
 
 No comments were made on the Revenue Report as presented. 
 
 Announcement was made of a Public Hearing to be held January 12, 2026 at 6:00 p.m. in

meeting, to determine whether compliance of annexation conditions required by Wyoming Statute 
§ 15-1-402 exist for the City- initiated annexation of 26 parcels of land totaling roughly 279.98 
acres comprised of various tracts of land situate in north Cheyenne generally located south of 
Storey Boulevard, east of Powderhouse Road, north of Dell Range Boulevard, and west of Ridge 
Road. 
 
 Announcement of a Public Hearing to be held January 12, 2026 at 6:00 p.m. in City Council 
Chambers, 2101 O’Neil Avenue, Cheyenne, WY, and via electronic conference meeting, for a 
transfer of ownership of retail liquor license application filed with the City Clerk’s Office for Ace’s 
Range LLC d/b/a Ace’s Range, 1505 Pioneer Ave., Cheyenne, WY (license currently held by F & 
G Corporation d/b/a The Green Door). 
 
The following announcement was introduced under Other Business: Announcement of a 
Public Hearing to be held January 12, 2026 at 6:00 p.m. in City Council Chambers, 2101 O'Neil 
Avenue, Cheyenne, WY, and via electronic conference meeting, for a transfer of ownership of 
retail liquor license application filed with the City Clerk's Office for Westby Edge LLC d/b/a 
Westby Edge Brewing, 714 W. 20th St., Cheyenne, WY (license currently held by Scooters 
Scoreboard Inc.).    
 
Public comment was made by the following under Other Business:  Natalie Lanzi and 
Brandon Swain.  The following members of the governing body made comments under Other Business: Dr. 
Aldrich, Mayor Collins, Dr. Emmons, Mr. Esquibel, Mr. Laybourn, Mr. Moody, Mr. White and 
Mr. Wolfe.  
 
There being no further business to come before the governing body, the meeting was 
officially adjourned at 6:56 p.m. 
 
        Submitted by, 
 
              
        Kylie Soden, 
        City Clerk

Mr. Segrave moved to meet in Executive Session pursuant to Wyoming Statute §16- 4-

at 6:00 p.m. in City Council Chambers  and via electronic conference meeting. Present were:

February 9, 2026 
 
The Governing Body of the City of Cheyenne met in regular session on this date beginning 
at 6:00 p.m. in City Council Chambers  and via electronic conference meeting. Present were: 
MAYOR – Patrick Collins, COUNCIL MEMBERS – Dr. Michelle Aldrich (via Zoom), Dr. Kathy 
Emmons, Ken Esquibel, Pete Laybourn, Mark Moody, Dr. Mark Rinne (via Zoom), Tom Segrave, 
Jeff White and Lawrence Wolfe. Also present: Kylie Soden, City Clerk. The pledge of allegiance 
was recited. 
 
Consent Agenda. (All agenda items listed with the designation of [CA] are considered to be

normal sequence on the agenda). Upon request by Mr. Laybourn, and pursuant to support received

“yes” – all members of the governing body.

and southern Cheyenne generally located east of I -25, south of the intersection of Westland Rd.

Kim Stevens, Tat iana M., Charles Miller and Erin Edwards . Comments were made by the 
following members of the governing body:  Dr. Aldrich, Mayor Collins, Dr. Emmons, Mr. 
Esquibel, Mr. Laybourn, Mr. Moody, Dr. Rinne, Mr. White and Mr. Wolfe . There being no further 
comments or input and the purpose of the public hearing having been met, Mayor Collins closed 
the public hearing.  
 
 Following a brief recess, Mayor Collins reconvened the meeting at 8:16 p.m. 
   ORDINANCE –3rd READING – Creating Chapter 1.28, Administrative Inspection 
Warrants, establishing authority for their issuance, and amending the Municipal Code of the City 
of Cheyenne, Wyoming, to authorize certain city officials, as specified, to apply for administrative

dated February 5 , 2026 , seconded by Mr. Segrave. Dr. Aldrich moved to amend  section 
1.28.020(b)(2) to replace the first “or” with “and” to read “There is probable cause to believe that 
a condition of nonconformity, violation or other circumstance requiring corrective action exists 
with respect to the designated property and  that causes an immediate risk to public health or 
safety”, seconded by Mr. Moody. Motion to amend  failed. Voting “no” – all members of the 
governing body with the exception of Dr. Aldrich and Mr. Moody voting “yes”. Dr. Aldrich moved 
to amend section 1.28.020(b)(3)  to remove “determine, discover or ”, seconded by Mr. Moody. 
Motion to amend carried. Voting “yes” Dr. Aldrich, Mayor Collins, Mr. Esquibel, Mr. Moody, Dr. 
Rinne and Mr. White. Voting “no” - Dr. Emmons, Mr. Laybourn, Mr. Segrave and Mr. Wolfe. Mr. 
Moody moved to amend section 1.28.020(b)(1) to add “For the purpose of this ordinance, area is 
defined as any large open space in a single commercial or abandoned property, and includes 
gathering areas, open office space, parking areas, and the exterior environment of the single parcel 
within which the single commercial or abandoned property resides”, seconded by Dr. Aldrich. Mr. 
Wolfe raised a point of order  regarding Mr. Moody’s proposed amendment , stating that verbal 
amendments are not an efficient way to approach amendments. Mayor Collins responded that, 
under Robert’s Rules of Order, verbal amendments are permitted; however, as a courtesy, 
providing amendments in writing would be beneficial in the future. Motion to amend failed. Voting 
“no” – all members of the governing body with the exception of Dr. Aldrich and Mr. Moody voting 
“yes”. Motion to amend by substitute, as amended carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the 
governing body. Main motion as amend ed by substitute, as amended carried. Voting “yes” – all 
members of the governing body with the exception of Mr. Esquibel, Mr. Moody and Dr. Rinne 
voting “no”. Public comment was made by: Patricia McCoy, Exie Brown, Kathy Scigliano, Bailey 
Turner, Mr. Matthews, Gary Chadwick, Charles Miller, Steven Love, Tamara Trujillo, Al an 
Sheldon and Kristen Turner . Comments were made by the following members of the governing 
body: Dr. Aldrich, Mayor Collins, Dr. Emmons, Mr. Laybourn, Mr. Moody, Dr. Rinne  and Mr. 
Wolfe. (#4656) 
 
 ORDINANCE – 3rd READING – Annexing to the City of Cheyenne, Wyoming, various

and west of Ridge Road. Dr. Emmons moved to approve on third and final  reading, seconded by 
Mr. Segrave. Motion carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body. Comment was

carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body. (#4658) 
   ORDINANCE – 3rd READING – Amending 5.7.3 Accessory Dwelling Units of the 
Cheyenne Unified Development Code to remove owner -occupancy and adjust parking 
requirements for Accessory Dwellings, and making conforming amendments to the definitions of 
an Accessory Dwelling and Semi -Attached Dwelling under 1.4.4 Descriptions of Uses of Land 
and Buildings. Dr. Emmons moved to approve on third and final reading, seconded by Mr. Moody. 
Motion carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body with the exception of Dr. Rinne

by the following members of the governing body: Mr. Moody and Dr. Rinne. (#4659)

Emmons advised there was no recommendation from Public Services Committee. Dr. Emmons 
moved to approve on second reading, seconded by Mr. White . Dr. Aldrich moved to postpone to

members of the governing body with the exception of Dr. Emmons voting “no”. Comments were 
made by the following members of the governing body:  Dr. Aldrich, Dr. Emmons, Mr. Esquibel, 
Mr. Laybourn, Dr. Rinne and Mr. Wolfe.  
 
 ORDINANCE – 1st READING – Amending the Official Zoning Map of the City of 
Cheyenne, changing the zoning classification for certain land located north of Prairie Avenue, east 
of Powderhouse Road, west of Rue Terre, and south of Storey Boulevard from AG – Agricultural 
to NR -3 – Neighborhood Residential High Density – referred to Public Services Committee . 
(Sponsor – Dr. Emmons)

Cheyenne, changing the zoning classification for land located southeast of the intersection of South 
Greeley Highway and East Dayshia Lane from AG – Agricultural to BP – Business Park – referred

Cheyenne generally located east of I -25, south of the intersection of Westland Road and Missile 
Drive, north of West and East Allison Road, and east of and adjacent to North College Drive  –

[CA] RESOLUTION – Expressing the support of the Governing Body for the inclusion of

Office of City Clerk 
 
February 23, 2026 
 
The Governing Body of the City of Cheyenne met in regular session on this date beginning 
at 6:00 p.m. in City Council Chambers  and via electronic conference meeting. Present were: 
MAYOR – Patrick Collins, COUNCIL MEMBERS – Dr. Michelle Aldrich, Dr. Kathy Emmons, 
Ken Esquibel, Pete Laybourn, Mark Moody, Dr. Mark Rinne, Tom Segrave (via Zoom), Jeff White 
and Lawrence Wolfe. Also present: Kylie Soden, City Clerk. The pledge of allegiance was recited. 
 
Consent Agenda. (All agenda items listed with the designation of [CA] are considered to be 
routine items by the governing body and will be enacted by one motion. There will be no separate 
discussion on these items unless a member of the governing body so requests and support by two 
other members is received.  Any item removed from the Consent Agenda will be considered in its 
normal sequence on the agenda). Upon request by Mr. Esquibel, and pursuant to support received 
by Dr. Aldrich and Mr. Moody, items #19(a) and #19(b) were removed from the Consent Agenda.  
Upon request by Mr. Moody, and pursuant to support received by Dr. Aldrich and Mr. White, item 
#14 was removed from the Consent Agenda.  Dr. Aldrich  moved to approve  remaining items , 
seconded by Mr. White. Motion carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body. 
 
[CA] Minutes from Regular Meeting of the Governing Body on February 9, 2026. Motion (per 
Consent Agenda) carried. 
 
 Mayor Collins opened a public hearing  for renewal applications for existing City liquor 
licenses (retail, restaurant, limited retail, resort, bar and grill licenses, microbrewery, satellite 
distillery, special malt beverage and winery permits) filed with the City Clerk’s Office. Public 
comments were made by: A.K. Wallace and Cameron Brown, Cheba Hut. There being no further 
comments or input and the purpose of the public hearing having been met, Mayor Collins closed 
the public hearing and referred the applications to the Finance Committee.  
 
 ORDINANCE – 2nd READING – Creating Chapter 8.72, Private Displays on Public 
Property, to prohibit the unauthorized use of public property for specified private displays . 
Reporting for Public Services Committee,  Dr. Rinne moved to approve on second reading, 
seconded by Dr. Aldrich . Dr. Aldrich moved to amend by substitute dated February 13, 2026, 
seconded by Mr. Moody . During comments made by Dr. Emmons regarding the substitute, Dr. 
Aldrich raised a point of order that comments were off subject.  Mayor Collins responded that the 
comments were germane to the substitute. Motion to amend by substitute carried. Voting “yes” – 
all members of the governing body with the exception of Dr. Emmons  voting “no”. Main motion 
as amended by substitute carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body with the 
exception of Dr. Emmons and Dr. Rinne voting “no”. Public comments were made by: Cheryl 
Gerrish and Steven Love. Comments were made by the following members of the governing body: 
Dr. Aldrich, Mayor Collins, Dr. Emmons, Mr. Esquibel, Mr. Moody, Dr. Rinne and Mr. Wolfe. 
   ORDINANCE – 2nd READING – Amending the Official Zoning Map of the City of 
Cheyenne, changing the zoning classification for certain land located north of Prairie Avenue, east 
of Powderhouse Road, west of Rue Terre, and south of Storey Boulevard from AG – Agricultural 
to NR -3 – Neighborhood Residential High Density. Dr. Rinne moved to approve on second 
reading, seconded by Mr. Esquibel. Motion carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the governing 
body. Public comment was made by:  Andrew Schafer, R eal Estate Equities D evelopment 
Company. Comment was made by the following member of the governing body: Mayor Collins.  
 
 ORDINANCE – 2nd READING – Amending the Official Zoning Map of the City of 
Cheyenne, changing the zoning classification for land located southeast of the intersection of South 
Greeley Highway and East Dayshia Lane from AG – Agricultural to BP – Business Park. Dr. Rinne 
moved to approve on second reading, seconded by Mr. Moody. Motion carried. Voting “yes” – all 
members of the governing body. 
 
 ORDINANCE – 2nd READING – Annexing to the City of Cheyenne, Wyoming, various 
tracts of land completely surrounded by current City limits situate in western and southern 
Cheyenne, generally located east of I-25, south of the intersection of Westland Road and Missile 
Drive, north of West and East Allison Road, and east of and adjacent to North College Drive. Dr. 
Rinne moved to approve on second reading, seconded by D r. Aldrich. Dr. Aldrich moved to 
postpone to March 9, 2026, seconded by Mr. Moody. Motion to postpone failed. Voting “yes” – 
Dr. Aldrich, Mr. Esquibel, Mr. Moody and Mr. White. Voting “no” – Mayor Collins, Dr. Emmons, 
Mr. Laybourn, Dr. Rinne, Mr. Segrave and Mr. Wolfe. Mr. Moody moved to amend by removing 
Parcel 4  and the southern portion of P arcel 7 , seconded by Dr. Aldrich.  During comments  
regarding the amendment, Mayor Collins ruled David Kniseley out of order. Mr. Esquibel moved 
to divide the question to consider Parcel 4 and the southern portion of Parcel 7 separately, seconded 
by Dr. Aldrich. Dr. Rinne raised  a point of order regarding the motion to divide the question, 
stating it was not divisible. Mayor Collins ruled the motion  was in order. Motion to divide the 
question failed. Voting “yes” – Dr. Aldrich, Mr. Esquibel, Mr. Moody and Mr. White. Voting “no” 
– Mayor Collins, Dr. Emmons, Mr. Laybourn, Dr. Rinne, Mr. Segrave and Mr. Wolfe.  
 
 Following a brief recess, Mayor Collins reconvened the meeting at 7:40 p.m. 
 
 Mr. Moody, with concurrence by Dr. Aldrich as the second to the motion, moved by 
friendly amendment to remove Parcels 4 and 7 in their entirety. Motion to amend failed. Voting 
“no” all members of the governing body with the exception of Mr. Esquibel and Mr. Moody voting 
“yes”.  Main motion carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body with the exception 
of Mr. Esquibel and Mr. Moody voting “no”. Public comments were made by: David Kniseley, 
WYFresh, Donald Crerar, Steven Love, Brian Pixley, Richard Knis eley, Micah Sutton, Chelsea 
McCort, Alan Sheldon and Tommy Kniseley, WYFresh . Comments were made by the following 
members of the governing body:  Dr. Aldrich, Mayor Collins, Dr. Emmons, Mr. Esquibel, Mr. 
Laybourn, Mr. Moody, Dr. Rinne, Mr. Segrave, Mr. White and Mr. Wolfe. 
 
 ORDINANCE – 2nd READING – Amending the Official Zoning Map of the City of 
Cheyenne, establishing the zoning classifications of AG – Agricultural, MR – Medium-Density 
Residential, CB – Community Business, and LI – Light Industrial, for land annexed to the City of 
Cheyenne generally located east of I -25, south of the intersection of Westland Road and Missile  Drive, north of West and East Allison Road, and east of and adjacent to North College Drive. Dr. 
Rinne moved to approve on second reading, seconded by Dr. Aldrich. Motion carried. Voting 
“yes” – all members of the governing body. 
 
 ORDINANCE –1st READING – Repealing and replacing Ordinance No. 4603, specifying 
the monthly Stormwater Runoff Management System user fee in accordance with Section 
13.32.050 of the Municipal Code of the City of Cheyenne, Wyoming, and providing a revised 
effective date – referred to Finance Committee. (Sponsors – Dr. A ldrich, D r. E mmons, M r. 
Esquibel, Mr. Laybourn, Mr. Moody, Dr. Rinne, Mr. Segrave, Mr. White and Mr. Wolfe) 
 
[CA] RESOLUTION – Expressing the support of the Governing Body for the inclusion of 
Laramie County Property ID Number 14663133500500 in the Downtown Development District . 
Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried. (#6514) 
 
 RESOLUTION – Authorizing the Mayor and City Clerk to sign a final plat for Village 
Cooperative, City of Cheyenne, Laramie County, Wyoming (located north of Prairie Avenue, east 
of Powderhouse Road, west of Rue Terre, and south of Storey Boulevard) . Dr. Rinne moved to 
adopt, seconded by Mr. Wolfe. Dr. Rinne moved to postpone to March 9, 2026, seconded by Mr. 
Wolfe. Motion to postpone carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body. Comment 
was made by the following member of the governing body: Mayor Collins. 
 
[CA] RESOLUTION – Directing the deposit of proceeds from the sale of certain real property 
into the City’s Real Property Revolving Fund – referred to Finance Committee . (Sponsor – Mr. 
Esquibel) 
 
[CA] RESOLUTION – Authorizing the submission of an Americorps Seniors Foster 
Grandparent Program application to Americorps on behalf of the Governing Body of the City of 
Cheyenne for a three-year continuation of funding for the Youth Alternatives Foster Grandparent 
Program and related support items – referred to Finance Committee. (Sponsor – Mr. Esquibel) 
 
[CA] RESOLUTION – Authorizing the Cheyenne Board of Public Utilities to execute a grant 
agreement with the Wyoming Office of Homeland Security for Federal Emergency Management 
Agency Rehabilitation of High Hazard Potential Dams funding and to authorize the Dire ctor of 
the Board to execute all related documents  – referred to Finance Committee. (Sponsor – Dr. Rinne) 
 
[CA] RESOLUTION – In support of the Professional Rodeo Cowboy Association (PRCA) and 
Professional Rodeo Hall of Fame and Museum of the American Cowboy  – referred to Finance 
Committee. (Sponsors– Dr. Aldrich, Dr. Emmons, Mr. Esquibel, Mr. Laybourn, Mr. Moody, Dr. 
Rinne, Mr. Segrave, Mr. White and Mr. Wolfe) 
 
  Professional Services Agreement between the City of Cheyenne and TDSi for professional 
design services for the repurposing of the Historic Pumphouse (General Fund Reserves). Reporting 
for Finance Committee, Mr. Esquibel moved to approve in an amount not to exceed $198,903.00, 
seconded by Mr. White. Mr. Wolfe moved to amend by substitute dated February 20, 2026, 
seconded by Mr. Moody. Motion to amend by substitute carried. Voting “yes” – all members of 
the governing body. Main motion as amended by substitute carried. Voting “yes” – all members  of the governing body.  Public comments were made by:  Maren Kallas, Historic Cheyenne Inc., 
Milward Simpson and Randy Byers, TDSi. Comment s were made by the following member s of 
the governing body: Mayor Collins, Mr. Laybourn, Mr. Moody, Dr. Rinne and Mr. Wolfe. (#8317) 
 
  Utility Easement Agreement between the City of Cheyenne and Microsoft Corporation for 
grant of perpetual right-of-way and temporary easement for underground fiber lines  (Revenue to 
the City). Mr. Esquibel moved to approve in an amount of $10.00, seconded by Mr. White . Mr. 
Esquibel moved to amend in the amount of $1,265.00, seconded by Mr. White. Motion to amend 
carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body. Main motion as amended carried. 
Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body with the exception of Mr. Moody voting “no”. 
(#8318) 
 
[CA]  Contract Modification #3 to Contract #7977 between the City of Cheyenne and Simon

Fleet Maintenance Fund & Solid Waste Fund). Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried (in an amount

[CA]  Contract Modification #1 to Contract #7821 between the City of Cheyenne and United

community programs (2019-2022 Optional 1% Sales Tax Fund) . Motion (per Consent Agenda) 
carried. (#7821) 
 
[CA] Contract Modification #1 to Contract #7322 between the City of Cheyenne and Sweetgrass 
Homeowners Association and the Sweetgrass Commercial Owners Association to outline 
responsibilities for both construction and maintenance of the Greater Cheyenne Greenway as well 
as enhanced landscaping constructed within tracts of land owned by the City and for areas within 
the public right-of-way within Sweetgrass, 1st and 2nd Filings – referred to Finance Committee. 
 
[CA]  Consideration of Bid #S-9-26 for an Agreement between the City of Cheyenne and Aztec 
Construction Co., Inc., for the Kiwanis Park Trail and Constructed Wetlands project (2017 Specific 
Purpose Tax Fund & Wyoming Department of Environmental Quality Grant) . Motion (per

[CA]  Consideration of Bid #E-8-26 for furnishing One (1) New 52K GVWR Truck with Trash

[CA]  Consideration of Bid #E -12-26 for furnishing One (1) New Recycling Vacuum & High

 No comments were made on the Revenue Report as presented. 
  
Public comment was made by the following under Other Business: Ted Hanlon. 
 
The following members of the governing body made comments under Other Business: Dr.

Mr. Laybourn moved to meet in Executive Session pursuant to Wyoming Statute §16- 4-

RECORD OF PROCEEDINGS FOR THE GOVERNING BODY 
OF THE CITY OF CHEYENNE 
 
Office of City Clerk 
 
March 5, 2026 
 
 The Governing Body of the City of Cheyenne convened in a special meeting on this date 
beginning at 6:00 p.m. in City Council Chambers for the purpose of collective labor bargaining 
with the Cheyenne Professional Fire Fighters, International Association of Fire Fighters, Local 
No. 279.  Present were:  MAYOR – Patrick Collins; COUNCIL MEMBERS – Mr. Esquibel, Mr. 
Laybourn, Mr. Moody, Mr. Segrave (via Zoom), Mr. White and Mr. Wolfe. Absent:  Dr. Aldrich, 
Dr. Emmons and Dr. Rinne . Also present: Kylie Soden, City Clerk; John Brodie, City Attorney; 
Amber Ash, Mayor’s Chief of Staff; Robin Lockman, City Treasurer and Chief Andrew Dykshorn 
and Deputy Chief Don Wood, Cheyenne Fire Rescue.  The pledge of allegiance was recited. 
      
 Mayor Collins advised he would entertain a motion to go into executive session.  Pursuant 
to Wyoming State Statute §16 -4-405(a)(x), Mr. Wolfe moved to meet in executive session, 
seconded by Mr. Esquibel.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body 
present. The following staff members were in attendance: Amber Ash, Mayor’s Chief of Staff; 
John Brodie, City Attorney; Robin Lockman, City Treasurer; Kylie Soden, City Clerk  and Chief 
Andrew Dykshorn and Deputy Chief Don Wood, Cheyenne Fire Rescue. [City Clerk note: audio 
and video recording of the special meeting was stopped; Executive Session convened at 6:05 p.m. 
in the Mayor’s conference room] 
 
Following closure of the executive session, Mayor Collins reconvened the special meeting 
at 6:40 p.m.  
 
Chris Thoms, President, Local #279, expressed appreciation for the labor -management 
meetings that take place in advance of contract negotiation meetings. He stated the Union’s 
primary goal is to address firefighter wages and presented wage comparisons for firefighter 
positions in Wyoming, Colorado, Montana, and South Dakota. Mr. Thoms indicated it is the 
Union’s position that Cheyenne firefighter compensati on falls behind regional standards. Upon a 
request for clarification on the jurisdictions used for wag e comparisons , Mr. Thoms provided 
additional information and stated that Cheyenne competes with departments along the Front 
Range. Mayor Collins stated that Wyoming communities are the most appropriate peer 
comparisons and noted the City has not experienced significant recruitment or retention issues in 
recent years. Mr. Thoms indicated the Union’s analysis includes both starting and top -out wages 
and that Cheyenne falls behind some communities in top-out compensation. 
 
Discussion continued regarding differences in municipal funding structures, statewide 
compensation averages, top-out wages, identification of appropriate peer communities with similar 
tax structures and populations, and the number of applicants for entry-level firefighter positions. 
 
      Submitted by, 
 
 
       Kylie Soden, 
       City Clerk   This notice is available in alternative, accessible formats upon request. 
 
Published: Wyoming Tribune-Eagle 
  March 11, 2026

RECORD OF PROCEEDINGS FOR THE GOVERNING BODY 
OF THE CITY OF CHEYENNE 
 
Office of City Clerk 
 
March 12, 2026 
 
 The Governing Body of the City of Cheyenne convened in a special meeting on this date 
beginning at 6:00 p.m. in City Council Chambers for the purpose of collective labor bargaining 
with the Cheyenne Professional Fire Fighters, International Association of Fire Fighters, Local 
No. 279.  Present were:  MAYOR – Patrick Collins; COUNCIL MEMBERS – Dr. Aldrich, Dr. 
Emmons, Mr. Esquibel, Mr. Laybourn, Mr. Moody, Mr. Segrave, Mr. White  and Mr. Wolfe . 
Absent: Dr. Rinne. Also present: Kylie Soden, City Clerk; John Brodie, City Attorney;  Amber 
Ash, Mayor’s Chief of Staff;  Robin Lockman, City Treasurer and Chief Andrew Dykshorn , 
Deputy Chief Don Wood and Deputy Chief of Administrative Services, Glenn Rodgers, Cheyenne 
Fire Rescue.  The pledge of allegiance was recited. 
      
 Mayor Collins advised he would entertain a motion to go into executive session.  Pursuant 
to Wyoming State Statute §16 -4-405(a)(x), Mr.  Segrave moved to meet in executive session, 
seconded by Mr. White.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body 
present. The following staff members were in attendance: Amber Ash, Mayor’s Chief of Staff; 
John Brodie, City Attorney; Robin Lockman, City Treasurer; Kylie Soden, City Clerk  and Chief 
Andrew Dykshorn, Deputy Chief Don Wood and Deputy Chief of Administrative Services, Glenn 
Rodgers, Cheyenne Fire Rescue.  [City Clerk note: audio and video  recording of the special 
meeting was stopped; Executive Session convened at 6:04 p.m. in the City Council office] 
 
Following closure of the executive session, Mayor Collins reconvened the special meeting 
at 6:33 p.m.  
 
Chris Thoms, President of Local #279, expressed appreciation for the Governing Body’s 
support and positive relationship with the Union. He briefly reviewed the Union’s request, noting 
that no wage increase was requested last year and emphasiz ed the need to remain competitive 
within the regional market. Mayor Collins thanked the Union for its constructive relationship with 
the City and acknowledged their concerns. He noted the importance of identifying an appropriate 
peer group for compensation comparisons and provided an overview of benefits offered in 
Cheyenne compared to other Wyoming communities, including retirement , wages and specialty 
and longevity pay. Mayor Collins stated that, in many cases, Cheyenne’s compensation is more 
favorable and noted that working in other states can involve  a higher cost of living due to factors 
including income and property taxes. He also provided a brief overview of the City’s proposal.  
Mr. Thoms requested a recess at 6:43 p.m., and Union members vacated chambers to the H R 
conference room to caucus. 
 
Mayor Collins reconvened the special session at 7:11 p.m., at which time it was agreed to 
adjourn until the next meeting. 
 
 There being no further business to come before the governing body, the meeting was 
officially adjourned at 7:12 p.m. 
 
        Submitted by, 
 
 
       Kylie Soden, 
       City Clerk 
 
 This notice is available in alternative, accessible formats upon request. 
 
Published: Wyoming Tribune-Eagle 
  March 18, 2026

RECORD OF PROCEEDINGS FOR THE GOVERNING BODY 
OF THE CITY OF CHEYENNE 
 
Office of City Clerk 
 
March 16, 2026 
 
 The Governing Body of the City of Cheyenne convened in a special meeting on this date 
beginning at 6:00 p.m. in City Council Chambers for the purpose of collective labor bargaining 
with the Cheyenne Professional Fire Fighters, International Association of Fire Fighters, Local 
No. 279.  Present were:  MAYOR – Patrick Collins; COUNCIL MEMBERS – Dr. Aldrich, Dr. 
Emmons, Mr. Esquibel, Mr. Laybourn, Mr. Moody, Mr. Segrave and Mr. White. Absent: Dr. Rinne 
and Mr. Wolfe. Also present: Kylie Soden, City Clerk; John Brodie, City Attorney; Amber Ash, 
Mayor’s Chief of Staff;  Robin Lockman, City Treasurer and Chief Andrew Dykshorn, Deputy 
Chief Don Wood  and Deputy Chief of Administrative Services, Glenn Rodgers, Cheyenne Fire 
Rescue.  The pledge of allegiance was recited. 
      
Chris Thoms, President of Local #279, emphasized the Union’s priority of maintaining fair 
market wages and noted that peer departments, including those along the Front Range, provide 
relevant comparisons. Jason Lindsay, Vice President of Local #279, presented pension and salary 
comparisons for firefighters in Wyoming, Colorado, and Montana. Discussion included specialty 
pay, Cheyenne’s economic growth,  and cost-of-living data sourced from bestplaces.net.  Mr. 
Thoms presented a counter proposal which included updates to Section 19 – Inclement Weather 
and Section 21 – Classification of Employment and Basic Wages. Additional discussion included 
recruitment efforts, attrition history, firefighter candidate pools, appropriate peer comparisons, the 
importance of aligning recurring revenues with recurring expenses, as well as the City’s use of 
reserves. 
 
Pursuant to Wyoming State Statute §16 -4-405(a)(x), Mr.  Segrave moved to meet in 
executive session, seconded by Mr. White.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the 
governing body present. The following staff members were in attendance: Amber Ash, Mayor’s 
Chief of Staff; John Brodie, City Attorney; Robin Lockman, City Treasurer; Kylie Soden, City 
Clerk and Chief Andrew Dykshorn, Deputy Chief Don Wood and Deputy Chief of Administrative 
Services, Glenn Rodgers, Cheyenne Fire Rescue. [City Clerk note: audio and video recording of 
the special meeting was stopped; Executive Session convened at 6:41 p.m. in the City Council 
office] 
 
Following closure of the executive session, Mayor Collins reconvened the special meeting 
at 7:06 p.m. and discussion continued regarding wage comparisons, specialty pay, and appropriate 
peer groups, including how comparable communities structure and fund compensation.  Mayor 
Collins expressed the belief that the City’s firefighters are not underpaid. Discussion also included 
cost-of-living comparisons among certain Wyoming communities, paramedic compensation and 
training considerations, and ongoing challenges in reaching an agreement on wage comparisons 
and the identification of appropriate peer groups. The City reiterated its standing offer related to 
wage increases. The Union requested adjournme nt to review rank average amounts provided by 
the City. 
 
 There being no further business to come before the governing body, the meeting was 
officially adjourned at 7:35 p.m.        Submitted by, 
 
 
       Kylie Soden, 
       City Clerk 
 
 This notice is available in alternative, accessible formats upon request. 
 
Published: Wyoming Tribune-Eagle 
  March 20, 2026

RECORD OF PROCEEDINGS FOR THE GOVERNING BODY 
OF THE CITY OF CHEYENNE 
 
Office of City Clerk 
 
March 17, 2026 
 
 The Governing Body of the City of Cheyenne convened in a special meeting on this date 
beginning at 6:00 p.m. in City Council Chambers for the purpose of collective labor bargaining 
with the Cheyenne Professional Fire Fighters, International Association of Fire Fighters, Local 
No. 279.  Present were:  MAYOR – Patrick Collins; COUNCIL MEMBERS – Dr. Aldrich, Dr. 
Emmons, Mr. Esquibel, Mr. Laybourn, Mr. Moody, Mr. Segrave and Mr. White. Absent: Dr. Rinne 
and Mr. Wolfe. Also present: Kylie Soden, City Clerk; John Brodie, City Attorney; Amber Ash, 
Mayor’s Chief of Staff;  Robin Lockman, City Treasurer and Chief Andrew Dykshorn, Deputy 
Chief Don Wood and Deputy Chief of Administrative Services, Glenn Rodgers, Cheyenn e Fire 
Rescue.  The pledge of allegiance was recited. 
      
Chris Thoms, President, Local #279, advised the parties remain at an impasse regarding 
wages and expressed a preference to proceed with reviewing other sections of the contract. Mayor 
Collins emphasized the City’s goal of maintaining Cheyenne Fire Rescue as the best place to work. 
He reviewed current staffing levels,  new fire stations, apparatus and equipment, and highlighted 
the City’s ongoing investments in firefighter safety. Mayor Collins expressed concern about losing 
momentum on progress made in negotiations and further reviewed compensation data, stating that 
Cheyenne firefighters are currently the highest paid in the state. He provided additional 
comparative information f or Loveland, CO , including staffing levels, call volumes per station, 
number of stations, battalion chief assignments, as well as cost of living considerations and noted 
that Loveland is not unionized. He reiterated that wages remain the primary point of concern  and 
expressed reluctance to move forward with other sections of the agreement at this time. Mr. Thoms 
requested a recess at 6:20 p.m., and Union members vacated chambers to the HR conference room 
to caucus. 
 
Mayor Collins reconvened the special session at 6:45 p.m. Mr. Thoms acknowledged that 
wages remain the primary issue and expressed the Union’s desire to continue moving forward with 
negotiations. Mayor Collins stated that the parties remain at a standstill pending agreement on 
certain key issues. Mr. Thoms requested that previously referenced data be provided for review in

RECORD OF PROCEEDINGS FOR THE GOVERNING BODY 
OF THE CITY OF CHEYENNE 
 
Office of City Clerk 
 
March 23, 2026 
 
 The Governing Body of the City of Cheyenne convened in a special meeting on this date 
beginning at 7:38 p.m. in City Council Chambers for the purpose of collective labor bargaining 
with the Cheyenne Professional Fire Fighters, International Association of Fire Fighters, Local 
No. 279.  Present were:  MAYOR – Patrick Collins; COUNCIL MEMBERS – Dr. Aldrich, Dr. 
Emmons, Mr. Laybourn, Mr. Moody, Dr. Rinne, Mr. Segrave, Mr. White and Mr. Wolfe. Absent: 
Mr. Esquibel. Also present: Luisa Walsh, Deputy City Clerk; John Brodie, City Attorney; Amber 
Ash, Mayor’s Chief of Staff; Robin Lockman, City Treasurer and Deputy Chief of Administrative 
Services, Glenn Rodgers, Cheyenne Fire Rescue.  The pledge of allegiance was recited. 
 
Mayor Collins provided opening remarks  regarding ongoing collective labor bargaining 
and acknowledged the concerns brought forth regarding salaries. He referenced a spreadsheet 
comparing the salaries of Local #279 to other departments throughout Wyoming and Colorado and 
emphasized we are comparable with other departments noting Cheyenne firefighters are offered 
reimbursement for education, whereas other departments do not offer this. Mayor Collins reviewed 
the City’s current compensation offer which includes maintaining the 3% COLA increase that was 
instituted in January, a 3% increase in base wage s, an additional 3.5% increase to Captain and 
4.75% to Battalion Chief to address compression, adjust probationary  firefighter step to 5% less 
than firefighter step 4 and increase medical, longevity and specialty pay by 3%. Chris Thoms,  
President, Local #279, requested a recess to review the proposal at 7:45 p.m., and Union members 
vacated chambers to the HR conference room to caucus. 
 
Mayor Collins reconvened the special session at 8:20 p.m. Mr. Thoms thanked the Mayor 
and City Council for their part in moving towards resolution. He stated that the Union was willing 
to move forward with the following framework: a ccept the 3% base pay increase with the 
understanding that it is a market base adjustment and not a COLA, an extension of the COLA 
sunset clause on page 34, Section 21 of the current Collective Labor Agreement to extend through 
the new ly proposed agreement, and  request City acceptance of the MERP  (Medical Expense 
Reimbursement Plan) language as proposed by the Union. Mayor Collins  reviewed the Vacation 
proposed language in Section 26 and advised that if the City and the  Union can agree to  the 
proposal, he would consider the MERP proposal. Mr. Thoms proposed amending the language to 
allow the four slots to be designated as either vacation or E.O.D. slots. Following discussion with 
Deputy Chief Rodgers, Mayor Collins confirmed mutual understanding of the vacation language, 
and both parties a greed to the revised terms  including MERP language . Regarding the MERP, 
Mayor Collins indicated general agreement, with the exception that the City would not be required 
to contribute for firefighters not actively working or contributing. Mr. Thoms concurred, and both 
parties approved the MERP language as presented by Ms. Ash. Discussion then turned to S ick 
Leave, Section 27, with agreement to allow day personnel to utilize sick leave. For accruals under 
Vacations, Section 26 #8, both parties agreed that a full month must be worked to qualify. 
Additional discussion addressed military leave and emergency leave scheduling under Vacations, 
Section 26 #7 and #8. Mr. Thoms proposed allowing daytime personnel to convert benefit hours 
using a correction factor; however, Mayor Collins declined due to differences between daytime  and platoon shifts. Mr. Thoms subsequently withdrew the request. Mayor Collins and Mr. Thoms 
announced acceptance of all terms as discussed. 
 
 There being no further business to come before the governing body, the meeting was 
officially adjourned at 8:36 p.m. 
      Submitted by, 
 
 
       Luisa Walsh, 
       Deputy City Clerk 
 
 This notice is available in alternative, accessible formats upon request. 
 
Published: Wyoming Tribune-Eagle 
  April 3, 2026

RECORD OF PROCEEDINGS FOR THE GOVERNING BODY 
OF THE CITY OF CHEYENNE 
Office of City Clerk 
 
April 13, 2026 
 
The Governing Body of the City of Cheyenne met in regular session on this date beginning 
at 6:00 p.m. in City Council Chambers  and via electronic conference meeting. Present were: 
MAYOR – Patrick Collins, COUNCIL MEMBERS – Dr. Michelle Aldrich, Dr. Kathy Emmons, 
Ken Esquibel, Pete Laybourn, Mark Moody, Dr. Mark Rinne (via Zoom), Tom Segrave, Jeff White 
and Lawrence Wolfe. Also present: Kylie Soden, City Clerk. The pledge of allegiance was recited.

routine items by the governing body and will be enacted by one motion. There will be no separate 
discussion on these items unless a member of the governing body so requests and support by two 
other members is received.  Any item removed from the Consent Agenda will be considered in its 
normal sequence on the agenda). Upon request by Mr. Segrave, and pursuant to support received 
by Dr. Aldrich and Mr. White, item #21 was removed from the Consent Agenda. Upon request by 
Mr. Laybourn, and pursuant to support received by Mr. Moody and Mr. Wolfe , item #22 was 
removed from the Consent Agenda. Upon request by Mr. Laybourn, and pursuant to support 
received by Dr. Aldrich and Mr. Moody, item #31(c) was removed from the Consent Agenda. Dr. 
Aldrich moved to approve remaining items, seconded by Mr. White. Motion carried. Voting “yes” 
– all members of the governing body.

Consent Agenda) carried.

Consent Agenda) carried.

Mr. White, and Mr. Wolfe. There being no further comments or input and the purpose of the public 
hearing having been met, Mayor Collins closed the public hearing.

Comments were made by the following members of the governing body:  Mayor Collins and Mr. 
White.

Fund). Mr. Esquibel advised that the item was reviewed under other business at the April 7, 2026, 
Finance Committee meeting, therefore, provisions of Title 2 of City Code have been met. Mr.

Cold Mix on an annual basis, for the City of Cheyenne, Street & Alley Division (2019- 2022 
Optional 1% Sales Tax Fund) – referred to Finance Committee. 
 
[CA] Consideration to Purchase between the City of Cheyenne and Musco Sports Lighting, LLC, 
for the purchase of a Mobile Video Trailer for the Community Recreation and Events Department 
(2023-2026 Optional 1% Sales Tax Fund, 2021 Specific Purpose Option Tax Fund and META 
Grant) – referred to Finance Committee. 
 
 
[CA] Application for a bar & grill liquor license application filed with the City Clerk’s Office 
for Mongolian Bar & Grill, d/b/a Mongolian Bar & Grill, 1637 Stillwater Ave. Ste. C, Cheyenne, 
WY. Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried. 
 
 No comments were made on the Voucher Report as presented.  
 
  Designation of the Official Voting Delegate and Alternate Delegate for the City of 
Cheyenne at the June 4, 2026 Wyoming Association of Municipalities Summer Convention 
Business Meeting to be held in Laramie, Wyoming. Mr. Esquibel moved to designate Dr. Mark 
Rinne as the Official Voting Delegate and Mayor Patrick Collins as the Alternate Delegate,  
seconded by Mr. White . Motion carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body.  
Comments were made by the following members of the governing body: Mayor Collins and Mr. 
Moody. 
 
Public comment s were made by the following under Other Business:  Noah Letcher , 
Southwest Regional Carpenters, and Charles Miller. 
 
The following members of the governing body made comments under Other Business: Dr. 
Aldrich, Mayor Collins, Mr. Esquibel and Mr. Moody. 
 
 
   Mr. Segrave moved to meet in Executive Session pursuant to Wyoming Statute §16- 4- 
405(a)(vii), seconded by Dr. Aldrich. Motion carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the governing 
body. Mayor Collins announced members would meet in executive session, not open to the public 
and stated there would be no action taken by the governing body as a result of the executive 
session, and that the regular City Council meeting would officially conclude at the close of the 
executive session. The following staff members w ere in attendance: Amber Ash, Mayor’s Chief 
of Staff; John Brodie, City Attorney; Robin Lockman, City Treasurer; and Kylie Soden, City 
Clerk.  
 
There being no further business to come before the governing body, the meeting was 
officially adjourned at 8:32 p.m.     
 
  
        Submitted by, 
 
              
        Kylie Soden, 
        City Clerk

minutes.text:
RECORD OF PROCEEDINGS FOR THE GOVERNING BODY 
OF THE CITY OF CHEYENNE 
Office of City Clerk 
 
April 27, 2026 
 
The Governing Body of the City of Cheyenne met in regular session on this date beginning 
at 6:00 p.m. in City Council Chambers  and via electronic conference meeting. Present were: 
MAYOR – Patrick Collins, COUNCIL MEMBERS – Dr. Michelle Aldrich, Dr. Kathy Emmons, 
Ken Esquibel, Pete Laybourn, Mark Moody, Dr. Mark Rinne  (arrived at 6:02 via Zoom), Tom 
Segrave, Jeff White and Lawrence Wolfe. Also present: Kylie Soden, City Clerk. The pledge of 
allegiance was recited. 
 
Consent Agenda. (All agenda items listed with the designation of [CA] are considered to be 
routine items by the governing body and will be enacted by one motion. There will be no separate 
discussion on these items unless a member of the governing body so requests and support by two 
other members is received.  Any item removed from the Consent Agenda will be considered in its 
normal sequence on the agenda). Upon request by Mr. Laybourn, and pursuant to support received 
by Mr. Moody and Mr. White, item #15 was removed from the Consent Agenda. Upon request by 
Mr. Laybourn, and pursuant to support received by Mr. Moody and Mr. Wolfe , item #29(a) was 
removed from the Consent Agenda. Upon request by Mr. Laybourn, and pursuant to support 
received by Dr. Aldrich and Mr. Moody, item #29(d) was removed from the Consent Agenda. Dr. 
Aldrich moved to approve remaining items, seconded by Mr. White. Motion carried. Voting “yes” 
– all members of the governing body. 
 
[CA] Minutes from Regular Meeting of the Governing Body on April 13, 2026 . Motion (per 
Consent Agenda) carried. 
 
 ORDINANCE – 3rd READING – Amending Section 13.20.050, General Prohibitions, and 
Section 13.20.070, Local Limits, of Chapter 13.20 Wastewater Treatment and Disposal, of the 
Code of the City of Cheyenne, Wyoming, to revise local discharge limits and related provisions in 
compliance with NPDES and WPDES permit requirements . Reporting for Public Services, Dr. 
Emmons moved to approve on third and final reading, seconded by Dr. Aldrich . Dr. Emmons 
moved to amend by substitute dated April 7, 2026, seconded by Dr. Aldrich. Motion to amend by 
substitute carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body. Dr. Emmons moved to 
postpone to May 11, 2026, seconded by Dr. Aldrich. Motion to postpone carried. Voting “yes” – 
all members of the governing body.   
 
 ORDINANCE – 3rd READING – Amending Section 2.76.040, designation of Downtown 
Development District, of Chapter 2.76, Downtown Development Authority, of Title 2, 
Administration and Personnel, of the Municipal Code of the City of Cheyenne, Wyoming, to 
expand the Downtown Development D istrict. Dr. Emmons moved to approve on third and final 
reading, seconded by Mr. White . Motion carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the governing 
body. (#4668) 
   ORDINANCE – 3rd READING – Appropriating money for the Reed Avenue Corridor 
Project. Reporting for Finance Committee, M r. Esquibel moved to approve on third and final 
reading, seconded by Mr. White . Motion carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the governing 
body with the exception of Mr. Moody voting “no”. [Clerk’s note: Due to technical issues, no vote 
was recorded for Dr. Rinne].  Public comment w as made by:  Jim Walter, Visit Cheyenne . 
Comments were made by the following members of the governing body:  Dr. Aldrich, Mr. 
Laybourn and Dr. Rinne. (#4669) 
 
 ORDINANCE –2nd READING – Amending the Official Zoning Map of the City of 
Cheyenne, changing the zoning classification for land located south of I -80, east of Southwest 
Drive from County LI Light Industrial, AG Agricultural, and AR Agricultural Residential to LI 
Light Industrial . Dr. Emmons moved to approve on second reading, seconded by Mr. W olfe. 
Motion carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body. 
 
 ORDINANCE – 2nd READING – Pursuant to Section 2.2.2 Planned Development –  
Regulating Plan or Development Master Plan and Section 5.6.2 PUD – Planned Unit Development 
District of the Unified Development Code, amending Ordinance No. 4524 by modifying certain 
standards of the adopted district, Plann ed Unit Development (PUD), for Sweetgrass (located 
southeast of the intersection of College Drive and Avenue C). Dr. Emmons advised there was no 
recommendation from Public Services Committee . Dr. Emmons moved to approve on second 
reading, seconded by Mr. Segrave. Motion carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the governing 
body. Public comments were made by: Casey Palma, Palma Land Planning and Charles Miller. 
Comments were made by the following members of the governing body: Dr. Aldrich, Mayor 
Collins and Mr. Moody. 
 
 ORDINANCE – 2nd READING – Annexing to the City of Cheyenne, Wyoming, land west 
of Roundtop Road and adjacent to Happy Jack Road. Dr. Emmons advised  there was no 
recommendation from Public Services Committee . Dr. Emmons moved to approve on second 
reading, seconded by Mr. Segrave . Dr. Emmons moved to amend by substitute dated April 15, 
2026, seconded by Mr. Segrave. Motion to amend by substitute  carried. Voting “yes” – all 
members of the governing body. Mr. Segrave moved to refer the ordinance to the Public Services 
Committee, and the c ommittee to be instructed to report at the June 8, 2026 c ouncil meeting, 
seconded by Dr. Emmons. Dr. Aldrich moved to amend by changing the date to the September 14, 
2026 council meeting, seconded by Dr, Emmons. Motion to amend carried. Voting “yes” – all 
members of the governing body. Motion to postpone as amended carried. Voting “yes” – all 
members of the governing body. During comments made by Charles Miller, Dr. Aldrich and Mr. 
White raised points of order that comments were off subject. Mayor Collins responded that 
comments were not germane to the subject . Public comments were made by: Cindy De Lancey, 
Holland and Hart , Tom Glissme yer, ViaWest Group, Gay Woodhouse , for Cox Ranch LLC, 
Heather Madrid, Jordan (no last name given), Conne r Nicklas, Falen Law Offices, representing 
land owner, Rick Keslar, Brendan Krachie, Thomas White, Sue Rocha, Brad Emmons, AVI, agent 
for applicant, Megan Plummer, Richard Lyle, Darrell Seifert, Alex Bowler , Cheyenne Area 
Landowners Coalition, Jack O’Neill, Skybox, Mark Eisele, King Ranch, Jane Lessenger , Sandy 
Walck, Sam Galeotos, Ann Margaret Burns, Michael White, Barry Meyer, Steve Johnson, Minda 
Blevins, Brian Pixley, Janet Tolman, Charles Miller, Chris Colson, Kathy Scigliano, Reba Eple r  and Mandie Shattuck. Comments were made by the following members of the governing body:  
Dr. Aldrich, Mayor Collins, Dr. Emmons, Mr. Esquibel, Mr. Moody, Mr. Segrave and Mr. Wolfe.  
 
 Following a brief recess, Mayor Collins reconvened the meeting at 8:55 p.m. 
 
 ORDINANCE –2nd READING –Amending the Official Zoning Map of the City of 
Cheyenne, establishing the zoning classification of AG – Agricultural and P – Public for land 
annexed to the City of Cheyenne located west of Roundtop Road and adjacent to Happy Jack Road. 
Dr. Emmons advised there was no recommendation from Public Services Committee. Dr. Emmons 
moved to approve on second reading, seconded by Mr. Segrave. Dr. Emmons moved to amend by 
substitute dated April 15, 2026, seconded by Mr. Segrave. Motion to amend by substitute carried. 
Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body. Mr. Segrave moved to refer the ordinance to 
the Public Services Committee, and the committee to be instructed to report at the September 14, 
2026 council meeting, seconded by Dr. Aldrich. Motion carried. Voting “yes” – all members of 
the governing body  with the exception of Dr. Rinne voting “no” . During comments made by 
Charles Miller regarding the postponement, Mr. Moody and Mr. White raised points of order that 
comments were off subject. Mayor Collins responded that comments were not germane to the 
postponement. Public comment was made by: Charles Miller.  Comment was made by the 
following member of the governing body: Dr. Rinne. 
  
 ORDINANCE –2nd READING – Amending the Official Zoning Map of the City of 
Cheyenne, changing the zoning classification for land located west of Roundtop Road and adjacent 
to Happy Jack Road from AG – Agricultural to BP – Business Park. Dr. Emmons advised there 
was no recommendation  from Public Services Committee . Dr. Emmons moved to approve  on 
second reading, seconded by Dr.  Aldrich. Mr. Segrave moved to refer the ordinance to the Public 
Services Committee, and the c ommittee to be instructed to report at the September 14, 2026 
council meeting, seconded by Dr. Aldrich. Motion carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the 
governing body with the exception of Dr. Rinne voting “no”. During comments made by Charles 
Miller regarding the postponement, Mr. Moody and Mr. Laybourn raised points of order that 
comments were off subject. Mayor Collins responded that comments were not germane to the 
postponement. Public comments were made by: Charles Miller, Jim Chiro and Chris Colson. 
Comments were made by the following members of the governing body:  Mayor Collins and Dr. 
Rinne. 
 
 ORDINANCE – 1st READING – Amending enforcement and permitting requirements 
related to Oversized Vehicles and making conforming amendments  – referred to Public Services 
Committee. (Sponsor – Dr. Emmons) 
 
 RESOLUTION – Approving a proposition to impose the 1% Specific Purpose Sales and 
Use Tax in Laramie County, State of Wyoming, for the exclusive purpose of funding specific 
purposes for specific amounts; the propositions to be voted on at the election to be held on August 
18, 2026. Mr. Esquibel moved to adopt, seconded by Mr. White . Motion carried. Voting “yes” – 
all members of the governing body. Comments were made by the following members of the 
governing body: Mr. Laybourn and Mr. Moody. (#6523) 
 
  [CA] RESOLUTION – Authorizing the Mayor and City Clerk to sign a Final Plat for Bison 
Apartments, City of Cheyenne, Laramie County, Wyoming, located north of West College Drive, 
east of Grand Harmony Boulevard, and west of Walterscheid Boulevard. Motion (per Consent 
Agenda) carried. (#6524) 
 
[CA] RESOLUTION – Authorizing the Mayor and City Clerk to sign a Final Plat for ONeil 
Edge, City of Cheyenne, Laramie County, Wyoming, located southwest of the intersection of West 
5th Street and O’Neil Avenue. Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried. (#6525) 
 
 RESOLUTION – Approving an increase of the budget of the Cheyenne Downtown 
Development Authority for the Fiscal Year beginning July 1, 2025, and ending June 30, 2026. Mr. 
Esquibel moved to adopt, seconded by Mr. White. Motion carried. Voting “yes” – all members of 
the governing body with the exception of Dr. Aldrich, Mr. Laybourn and Mr. Moody voting “no”. 
Public comments were made by: Alan Sheldon and Charles Miller. Comments  were made by the 
following members of the governing body:  Dr. Aldrich, Mayor Collins, Dr. Emmons and Mr. 
Moody. (#6526) 
 
[CA] RESOLUTION – Overruling the Planning Commission’s disapproval of an amendment to 
the Future Land Use Map of PlanCheyenne changing the land use designation from Mixed- Use 
Residential to Mixed -Use Employment for property generally located south of I -80, east of 
Southwest Drive. Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried. (#6527) 
 
[CA] RESOLUTION – Amending the Future Land Use Map of PlanCheyenne changing the land 
use designation from Mixed- Use Residential to Mixed -Use Employment for property generally 
located south of I-80, east of Southwest Drive. Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried. (#6528) 
 
[CA] RESOLUTION – Authorizing the Mayor and City Clerk to sign a Final Plat for Dry Creek 
Vista, City of Cheyenne, Laramie County, Wyoming (east of North College Drive and north of 
Rock Springs Street). Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried. (#6529) 
 
 RESOLUTION – Amending City provided health insurance related benefits for specified 
permanent part-time City employees and members of the City Council of the City of Cheyenne . 
Mr. Esquibel advised  there was no recommendation  from Finance Committee . Mr. Esquibel 
moved to adopt, seconded by Mr. Moody. Mr. Segrave called for the question, seconded by Dr. 
Emmons. Motion to call for the question carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the governing 
body. Main motion failed. Voting “no” – all members of the governing body with the exception 
of Dr. Aldrich and Mr. Mo ody voting “yes”.  Public comment was made by: Alan Sheldon. 
Comment was made by the following member of the governing body: Dr. Aldrich. 
 
[CA] RESOLUTION – Re-appropriating the Fiscal Year 2026 Budget of the City of Cheyenne 
in accordance with the provisions of W.S. §§ 16- 4-112 & 16- 4-113 – referred to Finance 
Committee. (Sponsor – Mr. Esquibel) 
 
 
  [CA] RESOLUTION – Amending the Future Land Use Map of PlanCheyenne changing the land 
use designation from Urban Transition Residential to Mixed- Use Employment for property 
generally located west of Roundtop Road and adjacent to Happy Jack Road and amending the 
Urban Service Boundary – referred to Public Services Committee. (Sponsor – Dr. Emmons) 
 
[CA] RESOLUTION – Appropriating excess funds from the November 2, 2021, One Percent 
(1%) Specific Purpose Sales and Use Tax for the acquisition of real property – referred to Finance 
Committee. (Sponsor – Dr. Aldrich) 
 
[CA] RESOLUTION – Adopting the Title VI Program for the Cheyenne Transit Program for the 
City of Cheyenne, Wyoming – referred to Finance Committee. (Sponsor – Mr. Esquibel) 
 
[CA] RESOLUTION – Expressing the support of the Governing Body for the submission of an 
application by the Cheyenne Transit Program to the Wyoming Department of Transportation for 
grant funding under the Wyoming Rural Public Transportation Grant  – referred to Finance 
Committee. (Sponsor – Mr. Esquibel) 
 
[CA] RESOLUTION – Approving the budget of the Cheyenne Downtown Development 
Authority for the fiscal year beginning July 1, 2026 and ending June 30, 2027 – referred to Finance 
Committee. (Sponsor – Mr. White) 
 
 Purchase and Sale Agreement between the City of Cheyenne and Nick and April Ferrulli, 
c/o NAS Investment Group, LLC for property located at 803 West 16th Street, 1510 Reed Avenue, 
1508 Reed Avenue and 1506 Reed Avenue for Greenway and Compliance use (2021 Specific 
Purpose Option Tax Fund and General Fund). Mr. Esquibel moved to approve in an amount not to 
exceed $650,000.00, seconded by Mr. White. Motion carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the 
governing body. During comments made by Charles Miller, multiple points of order were raised 
that comments were off subject. Mayor Collins responded that comments were not germane to the 
subject. Public comments were made by: Charles Miller, Alan Sheldon and Jim Chiro. Comments 
were made by the following members of the governing body:  Mayor Collins, Mr. Laybourn and 
Mr. Moody. (#8340) 
 
[CA] Drainage Easement Agreement between the City of Cheyenne and Christopher C. Post and 
Deborah L. Post, Trustees of the Post Revocable Trust for a recently constructed stormwater 
detention pond. Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried. (#8341) 
 
[CA] Professional Services Agreement between the City of Cheyenne and WM Recycle 
America, LLC for Recycling Services for the City of Cheyenne Sanitation Division (Solid Waste 
Fund). Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried (in an amount not to exceed $750,000.00 for 3 years). 
(#8342) 
 
 
 
 
   Grant Agreement between the City of Cheyenne and the U.S. Department of 
Transportation, Federal Transit Administration for a Section 5339(b) Competitive, and Section 
5339 Formula Grant for the Cheyenne Transit Facility Renovation at 1800 Westland Rd. (FTA 
Section 5339 Grant). Mr. Esquibel moved to approve in the amount of $4,143,600.00, seconded 
by Mr. Moody. Motion carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body. Comment was 
made by the following member of the governing body: Mr. Laybourn. (#8343) 
 
[CA] Grant Agreement between the City of Cheyenne and the U.S. Department of 
Transportation, Federal Transit Administration for a Section 5307 – Operating Assistance, ADA 
Paratransit Operating assistance, PM Vehicles/Facilities, & Capital Grant for the Cheyenne Transit 
System Program (FTA Section 5307 Grant). Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried (in an amount 
not to exceed $3,291,390.00). (#8344) 
 
[CA] Contract between the City of Cheyenne and BNSF Railway for a BNSF Railway and Grant 
Applicant 22905 Agreement for the Reed Avenue Rail Crossing Elimination Project (2017 
Specific Purpose Option Tax Fund) – referred to Finance Committee. 
 
[CA] Contract Modification #2 to Contract #7955 between the City of Cheyenne and Trihydro 
Corporation for Landfill Mapping and Surveying Services  (Solid Waste Fund ). Motion (per 
Consent Agenda) carried (in an amount not to exceed $49,008.00). (#7955) 
 
[CA] Contract Modification #1 to Contract #8259 between the City of Cheyenne and SPARE 
Labs Inc. for Transit Paratransit Dispatch System and new Fixed Route Tracking System (Transit 
Fund). Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried (in an amount not to exceed $78,000.00). (#8259) 
 
 Modification to Bid #E -4-25 for (3) Fire Apparatus for the City of Cheyenne, Cheyenne 
Fire Rescue Department  (General Fund Reserves and 2027 -2030 Specific Purpose Option Tax 
Fund). Mr. Esquibel advised the item was reviewed under other items for the agenda  at the April 
21, 2026 Finance Committee meeting, therefore, provisions of Title 2 of City Code had been met. 
Mr. Esquibel moved to approve with a savings of $44,035.06 on the original bid, seconded by Mr. 
Segrave. Motion carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body. Comments were 
made by the following members of the governing body: Dr. Aldrich and Mayor Collins. 
 
[CA] Contract Modification #1 to Contract #8218 between the C ity of Che yenne and AVI 
Engineering, PC for On -Call Engineering Services  (2022-2023 Optional 1% Sales Tax Fund)  – 
referred to Finance Committee.  
 
[CA] Consideration of Bid #S -20-26 for a Contract between the City of Cheyenne and 
Richardson Construction, Inc. for the Cheyenne Botanic Gardens -  Smith Education, Agriculture 
& Trial (E.A.T.) Garden (Friends of the Botanic Gardens). Motion  (per Consent  Agenda) carried 
(in an amount not to exceed $854,891.21). (#8345) 
 
[CA] Consideration of Bid #E-14-26 for furnishing Residential Automated Refuse Carts - 95/65 
Gallons, for the Sanitation Division (Solid Waste Fund) . Motion (per consent agenda)  carried 
(accepted bid from Rehrig Pacific Company in an amount not to exceed $204,884.00). 
  [CA] Consideration of Bid #E-15-26 for furnishing 1.5 Cubic Yard Rear -Load Dumpsters for 
the Sanitation Division  (Solid Waste Fund) . Motion (per consent agenda) carried (accepted bid 
from Kois Bros Equipment in an amount not to exceed $88,472.00). 
[CA] Consideration of Bid #E-17-26 for furnishing Bituminous Asphalt Hot Mix, Tack Oil, and 
Cold Mix on an annual basis, for the City of Cheyenne, Street & Alley Division (2019-2022 
Optional 1% Sales Tax Fund) . Motion (per consent agenda) carried (accepted bid from Simon 
Contractors for Bituminous Asphalt Hot Mix and Cold Mix in an amount not to exceed 
$495,750.00 and the bid from JTL Group Inc. d/b/a Knife River for Tack Oil  in an amount not to 
exceed $37,500.00, for a total of $533,250.00). 
 
[CA] Consideration to Purchase between the City of Cheyenne and Musco Sports Lighting, LLC, 
for the purchase of a Mobile Video Trailer for the Community Recreation and Events Department 
(2023-2026 Optional 1% Sales Tax Fund, 2021 Specific Purpose Option Tax Fund and META 
Grant). Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried (in an amount not to exceed $161,826.00).  
 
[CA] Consideration of Bid #S-19-26 for a Contract between the City of Cheyenne and Reiman 
Corp. for the Storey Boulevard Extension Construction project (2019- 2022 and 2023- 2026 
Optional 1% Sales Tax Fund) – referred to Finance Committee. 
 
[CA] Consideration of Bid #S -21-26 for a Contract between the City of Cheyenne and 
Construction Specialists, Inc. for the Cheyenne Transit Facility - Interior and Exterior Renovations 
and Upgrades project (Board of Public Utilities and Federal Transit Administr ation & WYDOT 
Grants)  – referred to Finance Committee. 
 
Appointment of Jason Powell, Brian Fenimore, and Paul Pomeroy to the Fire Code Board 
of Appeals; Justin Tripp to the Planning Commission; Cindy Orellana to the Housing and 
Community Development Advisory Council and Josephine Carlson to the Historic Preservation 
Board. Dr. Aldrich moved to approve, seconded by Mr. White. Motion carried. Voting “yes” – all 
members of the governing body with the exception of Mayor Collins  who did not vote (mayoral 
appointments). 
 
 No comments were made on the Voucher Report as presented. 
 
 No comments were made on the Revenue Report as presented.  
 
  Announcement was made of a Public Hearing to be held May 11, 2026 at 6:00 p.m. in City 
Council Chambers, 2101 O’Neil Avenue, Cheyenne, WY, and via electronic conference meeting, 
for a microbrewery permit application filed with the City Clerk’s Office for Jagerhund Brewing, 
LLC d/b/a Jagerhund Brewing, 3521 E. Lincolnway, Cheyenne, WY. 
 
Public comment s were made by the following under Other Business:  Jim Chiro, Alan 
Sheldon and Charles Miller. During comments made by Mr. Miller, Mayor Collins ruled him out 
of order, stating his remarks were not accurate in relation to previous agenda items. 
 
The following members of the governing body made comments under Other Business: Dr. 
Aldrich, Mayor Collins, Dr. Emmons, Dr. Rinne, Mr. Segrave, Mr. White and Mr. Wolfe. 
  There being no further business to come before the governing body, the meeting was 
officially adjourned at 10:06 p.m.     
  
        Submitted by, 
 
              
        Kylie Soden, 
        City Clerk

RECORD OF PROCEEDINGS FOR THE GOVERNING BODY 
OF THE CITY OF CHEYENNE 
Office of City Clerk 
 
May 11, 2026 
 
The Governing Body of the City of Cheyenne met in regular session on this date beginning 
at 6:00 p.m. in City Council Chambers  and via electronic conference meeting. Present were: 
MAYOR – Patrick Collins, COUNCIL MEMBERS – Dr. Michelle Aldrich, Dr. Kathy Emmons, 
Ken Esquibel, Pete Laybourn, Mark Moody, Dr. Mark Rinne , Jeff White and Lawrence Wolfe. 
Absent: Tom Segrave. Also present: Kylie Soden, City Clerk. The pledge of allegiance was recited. 
 
Consent Agenda. (All agenda items listed with the designation of [CA] are considered to be 
routine items by the governing body and will be enacted by one motion. There will be no separate 
discussion on these items unless a member of the governing body so requests and support by two 
other members is received.  Any item removed from the Consent Agenda will be considered in its 
normal sequence on the agenda).  Upon request by Dr. Emmons, and pursuant to support received 
by Dr. Aldrich and Mr. White, item #31(a) was removed from the Consent Agenda. Upon request 
by Mr. Laybourn, and pursuant to support received by Dr. Aldrich and Mr. Moody, item #30(a) 
was removed from the Consent Agenda. Mr. Esquibel  moved to approve  remaining items , 
seconded by Mr. White. M otion carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body  
present. 
 
[CA] Minutes from Regular Meeting of the Governing Body on April 27, 2026. Motion (per 
Consent Agenda) carried. 
 
Public Hearing was held for a microbrewery permit application filed with the City Clerk’s 
Office for Jagerhund Brewing, LLC d/b/a Jagerhund Brewing, 3521 E. Lincolnway, Cheyenne, 
WY. Public comment was made by: Fred Hirsch, Jagerhund Brewing. Comment s were made by 
the following members of the governing body: Mayor Collins  and Mr. Esquibel. There being no 
further comments or input and the purpose of the public hearing having been met, Mayor Collins 
closed the public hearing and referred the application to the Finance Committee. 
 
 ORDINANCE – 3rd READING – Amending Section 13.20.050, General Prohibitions, and 
Section 13.20.070, Local Limits, of Chapter 13.20 Wastewater Treatment and Disposal, of the 
Code of the City of Cheyenne, Wyoming, to revise local discharge limits and related provisions in 
compliance with NPDES and WPDES permit requirements . Reporting for Public Services  
Committee, Dr. Rinne moved to approve on third and final reading, seconded by Dr. Aldrich. Dr. 
Rinne moved to postpone to May 26, 2026, seconded by Dr. Aldrich. Motion to postpone carried. 
Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body present. 
 
 ORDINANCE – 3rd READING – Amending the Official Zoning Map of the City of 
Cheyenne, changing the zoning classification for land located south of I -80, east of Southwest 
Drive from County LI Light Industrial, AG Agricultural, and AR Agricultural Residential to LI 
Light Industrial. Dr. Rinne moved to approve on third and final reading, seconded by Mr. Wolfe .  Motion carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body present. Public comments were 
made by: John Niles and John Sayers, agent and applicant. (#4670) 
 
 ORDINANCE – 3rd READING – Pursuant to Section 2.2.2 Planned Development –  
Regulating Plan or Development Master Plan and Section 5.6.2 PUD – Planned Unit Development 
District of the Unified Development Code, amending Ordinance No. 4524 by modifying certain 
standards of the adopted district, Plann ed Unit Development (PUD), for Sweetgrass (located 
southeast of the intersection of College Dri ve and Avenue C). Dr. Rinne  advised there was no 
recommendation from Public Services Committee. Dr. Rinne moved to approve on third and final 
reading, seconded by Mr. Wolfe. Motion carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the governing 
body present. Public comments were made by: Casey Palma, Palma Land Planning, Charles Miller 
and Jim Chiro . Comments were made by the following members of the governing body:  Dr. 
Aldrich, Mayor Collins, Dr. Emmons, Dr. Rinne, Mr. White and Mr. Wolfe. (#4671) 
 
 ORDINANCE –2nd READING – Amending enforcement and permitting requirements 
related to Oversized Vehicles and making conforming amendments . Reporting for Finance 
Committee, Mr. Esquibel moved to approve on second  reading, seconded by Mr. White . Motion 
carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body present with the exception of Mr. 
Laybourn and Mr. Moody voting “no”. 
 
 ORDINANCE – 1st READING – Amending and updating the Solid Waste Fee Schedule 
in accordance with Section 8.44.010 of the Municipal Code of the City of Cheyenne, Wyoming, 
and repealing Ordinance No. 4621 – referred to Finance Committee. (Sponsor – Mr. Esquibel) 
 
 ORDINANCE – 1st READING – Amending the Official Zoning Map of the City of 
Cheyenne, changing the zoning classification for land located southwest of the intersection of HR 
Ranch Road and Judy Lee Drive, and southeast of HR Ranch Road and Judy Lee Drive, from JL 
Ranch PUD – Planned Unit Development to NR-2 Neighborhood Residential – Medium Density 
– referred to Public Services Committee. (Sponsor – Dr. Emmons)

Wyoming for the various purposes in conducting the Municipal Government of said city and fixing 
the amount of General and Special Taxes as part of the revenue required to meet the said 
appropriation, all for the Fiscal Year beginning July 1, 2026, and ending June 30, 2027 – referred 
to Committee of the Whole. (Sponsor – Mr. Segrave)

Committee. (Sponsor – Dr. Emmons)

and Septic and Commercial Waste Dump Rates, as recommended by the Board of Public Utilities 
– referred to Finance Committee. (Sponsor – Mr. Esquibel)   ORDINANCE – 1st READING – Imposing a temporary twelve (12) month moratorium on 
the establishment, construction, or conversion of any buildings or structures for use as a data 
center, including any change of use to a data center  – referred to Public Services Committee . 
(Sponsor – Mr. Moody)

carried. (#6530)

use designation from Urban Transition Residential to Mixed- Use Employment for property 
generally located west of Roundtop Road and adjacent to Happy Jack Road and amending the 
Urban Service Boundary. Dr. Rinne moved to adopt, seconded by Mr. Wolfe. Dr. Rinne moved to 
refer the resolution to the Public Services Committee, and the committee be instructed to report at 
the September 28, 2026 council meeting, seconded by Mr. White. Motion carried. Voting “yes” – 
all members of the governing body present. Public comment was made by: Michael White.

(1%) Specific Purpose Sales and Use Tax for the acquisition of real property. Motion (per Consent 
Agenda) carried. (#6531)

application by the Cheyenne Transit Program to the Wyoming Department of Transportation for 
grant funding under the Wyoming Rural Public Transportation Grant . Motion (per Consent 
Agenda) carried. (#6533)

Authority for the fiscal year beginning July 1, 2026 and ending June 30, 2027. Mr. Esquibel moved

governing body present. Main motion as amended carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the 
governing body present. Public comments were made by: Dave Teubner, Downtown Development 
Authority President and Charles Miller. Comments were made by the following members of the

raised points of order that comments were off subject. Public comment w as made by: Charles 
Miller. Comments were made by the following members of the governing body: Mayor Collins, 
Dr. Emmons, Mr. Laybourn, Dr. Rinne and Mr. White.

LLC for the Yellowstone Road and Dell Range Boulevard Rehabilitation and Traffic 
Improvements Project (2015-2018 Optional 1% Sales Tax Fund) – referred to Finance Committee.
